title: Mysore Palace
blurb: Henry Irwin’s 1912 Indo-Saracenic palace for the Wadiyars: a three-story granite block 75 m long, its five-story central tower crowned by a 44 m gold dome, with pink-domed corner towers.

systems.name: Main block
systems.description: The three-story granite main block, 75 m by 48 m, with plinth, walls, slabs and cornices.

systems.name: Central tower and gold dome
systems.description: The five-story central tower crowned by the 44 m gold-plated onion dome with its chhatri.

systems.name: Corner towers
systems.description: The four five-story square towers at the cardinal points, each with a pink dome.

systems.name: Arcades
systems.description: Arched bays on all four facades, the central entrance arch and the Gajalakshmi sculpture.

systems.name: Entrances
systems.description: The four named gates, the bronze tigers and the Elephant Gate.

systems.name: Roofs
systems.description: Roof slab, parapets and rooftop chhatris.

systems.name: Courtyard and gardens
systems.description: The inner courtyard and garden walls.
